title: Blue Mound Road, Milwaukee, and its pianists
summary: Wickliffe's band, with two violins, plays Blue Mound Road in Milwaukee. They try to name a local pianist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: It's strange that Wycliffe wasn't recorded.

I don't know why. Because we had a very good band. He always insisted. One good thing about him. He always insisted in getting good man. And he made the owners. They'd come up with, when they wanted to come up with that three or four or five pieces. He'd tell them, no, my band is eight, ten, whatever it was. And that's the way it sounds. And that's what's going to do your business. And he was a good talker in getting jobs. Because we went up to Blue Mountain. The Blue Chipper on the Blue Mountain Road, Milwaukee. We went up there. And we had two first violins. That was Clarence Lee and myself. We had a very good trumpeter. And we had Joe Walker, Lil' Joe Walker, playing Sykes. And Harry Gray, the president of our union, was up there. He was playing with us then. And I think he was playing tuba, if I'm not mistaken. Yes. Because I think he had got the bass fiddle later on. And Charlie Hillman was playing piano with us. He'd come up from Memphis. And...
Now, Jabba wasn't with you, was he?
No. He didn't play the Blue Mountain Road. Yes, but that was much later. Mm-hmm.

Wasn't too far from Sam Picks. Sam Picks. Yes. This is a great piano player. I forget his name was playing as Sam Picks, wasn't he? No. Lil' Walker's best colored piano player, they said. I forget his name.
But there was one piano player they played. He was called Lil' Walker's best piano player. I can't remember his name either.
